newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude dives on weak technicals, heating oil.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude dives on weak technicals, heating oil.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended sharply lower Thursday after violation major technical support compounded with bearish heating oil fundamentals to send oil prices into a tailspin.

"You are seeing prices taking their cue from a declining heating oil market which is in turn a function of weather being warmer than normal," said Michael Rothman, senior energy analyst with Merrill Lynch.
March crude settled off 81 cents at $23.10 a barrel.
"Falling through the $23.80 and $23.60 area was really what took us lower," said a New York crude trader.
Prompt crude had steadily held $23.80 throughout the week after last week's low of $23.63.
Sell stops were triggered beneath those levels Thursday, breaking a long-term trendline extending from the session low June 6 of $19.46 on a spot continuation chart.
Traders said March crude's settlement of $23.10 was near solid support between $23.05, March crude's simple 200-day moving average, and the psychological level of $23.00.
March heating oil declined 1.87 cents a gallon at 61.45 cents while March gasoline settled off 2.24 cents at 65.30 cents a gallon.
Oil prices declined for the fourth consecutive session, with a barrel of March crude dropping $1.90 in value since last Thursday.
Temperatures have trended above average all week in the northeastern United States, the largest heating oil market in the world.

Just when heat demand was suffering, the American Petroleum Institute (API) reported Tuesday that distillate stocks, comprised of heating oil and diesel, showed a surplus for the first time in more than a year.
Moreover, news earlier this week that a major market player had accepted more than two million barrels of heating oil for delivery increased concern over excess supply that would have to be sold.
Crude supplies were also said to be ample.
Output of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) hit a new 16-year high in January, swollen by Iraq's first full month of exports under the United Nations oil-for-food exchange.

Wellhead crude oil production from OPEC rose 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 26.64 million in January from a revised 26.34 million in December, a Reuter survey of oil analysts, OPEC delegates and company officials found.
Moreover, the API said its weekly data showed crude stocks rose six million barrels as of January 31.

"The evidence of increased supply, the uptick in crude inventories and the sharp downtrend in heating oil are all being reflected in the price today," said Tim Evans, analyst with Pegasus Econometric Research.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
